newsitem.title: UK: Glickman says US can support a grain subsidy battle.
newsitem.headline: Glickman says US can support a grain subsidy battle.

text.p: The United States has the political will and the cash to respond in kind to any excessive subsidies on grains by any competing world exporters, U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Friday.
He was talking to Reuters during a visit to a farm at Sittingbourne in southeast England after he had addressed a London annual conference of the International Grains Council (IGC).

"We have the resources to do it," Glickman said, restating a readiness - if other sellers push subsidies too hard - to bring the United States's export enhancement programme back into action after a pause of two years.
"We will fight fire with fire," he said.
But he declined to be drawn on what level of European Union farm export subsidies would trigger an aggressive U.S. response.

Glickman said he would prefer not to have to subsidise exports and he worried that differences over subsidies could "create non-agricultural political problems in countries which are otherwise allies."
